claims.text: Creep resistance in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy coatings is primarily governed by FCC/BCC interphase-boundary coherence and bonding strength.
More coherent FCC/BCC interfaces impede dislocation motion during sustained loading.
Strongly bonded FCC/BCC interfaces impede atomic diffusion during sustained loading.
The starting coating is a dual-phase FCC/BCC HEA produced under standard processing conditions.
The starting coating has variable interphase-boundary quality, including mixed degrees of coherency and bonding.
Tailoring solidification or additive-manufacturing cooling rates can systematically enhance FCC/BCC interface coherency and bonding strength.
Rapid quenching promotes relatively incoherent FCC/BCC boundaries.
Moderate cooling enhances FCC/BCC interface coherency.
High-resolution TEM, boundary-misfit measurements, bonding-strength measurements, and interface-energy measurements can quantify the proposed structural mediator.
Coherent and strongly bonded interphase boundaries act as pinning sites for dislocation glide.
Coherent and strongly bonded interphase boundaries slow atomic diffusion across the phases.
Restricting dislocation motion and diffusion-mediated strain accumulation decreases the creep rate under continuous high stress.
Coatings with greater interphase-boundary coherence will have a lower steady-state creep rate than baseline coatings under identical loading.
Coatings with greater interphase-boundary coherence will have a longer time to failure than baseline coatings.
Coatings with greater interphase-boundary coherence will exhibit less interphase sliding than baseline coatings.
Coatings with greater interphase-boundary coherence will exhibit less microstructural degradation than baseline coatings.
Mixed interface quality in standard-process coatings causes higher creep strain rates and faster progressive plastic deformation.
The proposed benefits are limited to sustained high-stress, elevated-temperature service conditions.
The proposed interface-controlled mechanism may be less effective at ambient temperature.
The proposed interface-controlled mechanism may be less effective when loading conditions cause phase instability.
